title: A clean job
direction: Adult American woman, early forties. Low chest register, lightly husky, sharp local East Coast consonants. You run jobs out of the back booth of a noisy diner, but the recording itself is clean and dry. You're talking to a cocky young crook seated two feet away, who keeps interrupting with stupid ideas. Throw away the opening as familiar business; get clipped and irritated on 'Don't count it, don't smell it'; 'for God's sake' is real exasperation, not elegant narration. Brief, cold amusement on 'Last fellow asked questions'. Drop your pitch and land 'Now I'm hiring you' as a pointed warning. Uneven conversational rhythm, contractions, a lived-in street voice. Do not make her posh, breathy, soothing, singsong, or theatrical. The humor comes from how little patience she has.
text: There's an envelope behind the counter at Halloway Gas. Bring it to me sealed. Don't count it, don't smell it, and for God's sake, don't ask the cashier what's inside. Last fellow asked questions. Now I'm hiring you.
